notes: Adopted 1983; adopted by all 50 US states + DC as basis for state bar rules. Previous model was 1969 Model Code.

document_title: SRA Code of Conduct for Solicitors, RELs and RFLs
notes: Part of SRA Standards and Regulations, in force November 2019. Separate Code of Conduct for Firms also exists.

document_title: BSB Handbook — Code of Conduct for Barristers
notes: 10 Core Duties for barristers. Enforced by the Bar Standards Board.
Collaboration of state/territory law societies. Adopted across Australian jurisdictions. Violation = unsatisfactory professional conduct or professional misconduct.

organization: Federation of Law Societies of Canada
notes: Adopted by all Canadian common law jurisdictions. Updated regularly by Standing Committee on Model Code. Current edition 2024.

document_title: International Principles on Conduct for the Legal Profession
notes: Adopted Warsaw 2011; updated 2018. 10 core principles providing framework for national codes globally.
Predecessor to 2011 International Principles. Originally adopted 1956, revised 1988. Retained as historical reference.

organization: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
notes: Current codified version effective December 15, 2014. Used by all US state boards of accountancy as model.

organization: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
notes: 2025 edition in force from 1 July 2025. Five fundamental principles: integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, professional behaviour.
ACCA adopts IESBA Code + supplementary requirements. Current version effective December 2024.

organization: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland
notes: Changes effective 1 January 2022, incorporating IESBA 2018 revisions. 2025 edition includes technology-related confidentiality changes.

organization: CPA Canada (Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada)
notes: Administered by provincial CPA bodies (CPA Ontario, CPABC, CPA Manitoba, etc.). Harmonised across Canada.

organization: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants
document_title: International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (including International Independence Standards)
notes: Revised and restructured 2018 edition came into effect June 2019. Underpins ICAEW, ACCA, ICAS, and all CCAB member body codes. 2024/2025 handbook available.

document_title: Code of Ethics / Global Internal Audit Standards (Domain II — Ethics and Professionalism)
notes: 2024 Global Internal Audit Standards integrate ethics as Domain II. Applies to all IIA members, certification holders, and internal audit practitioners.
Adopted January 1, 2001. Also adopted by CAS, ASPPA, and Conference of Consulting Actuaries. Enforced by Actuarial Board for Counseling and Discipline (ABCD).
IAA membership requires member associations to have codes of conduct, discipline processes, and educational standards.
Applies to all IMC USA members and Certified Management Consultants (CMC). Ethics Committee enforces via Rules of Procedure.

organization: International Council of Management Consulting Institutes
document_title: ICMCI Core Code of Ethics (minimum guidelines)
notes: International umbrella body for national IMC institutes and globally recognised certifying body for CMCs.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
notes: Updated version effective 17 November 2025. Four core values: responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty. Applies to all PMI members, volunteers, and certification holders.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
notes: First published 2015 (50th Anniversary); recently revised. Mandatory for all acting on behalf of IPMA.

organization: Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development
notes: Effective 1 January 2023. Replaced 2012 Code. Covers HR, L&D, OD professionals.

organization: Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply
notes: 64,000+ members in 180 countries. Breach may lead to disciplinary action under CIPS Royal Charter. Compliance required for Chartered Status.
First adopted 1914; major 2020 revision to stakeholder model (society, natural environment, profession, clients/employers, peers). First wholesale update since 1974.
Accompanied by 'Advice on Ethical Conduct' (2023 update). Applies to all ICE members globally.

organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
notes: First established 1963; revised periodically. Applies to all IEEE members worldwide (~400,000 members in 160+ countries).
By-laws and Code of Conduct apply to all IMechE members. Aligns with UK Engineering Council UK-SPEC ethical principles.
2024 edition modernised to include cyber security, sustainability, D&I, social media. Compliance is condition of IChemE membership.
Canons first published 1946; current Code adopted 1964. Board of Ethical Review issues written opinions on ethical cases. Six fundamental canons.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Guidelines on Professional Conduct
notes: 2022 edition. Four core values: integrity, competence, leadership, sustainability.
Released at General Assembly 14 October 2023. Designed to assist member organisations in formulating their own codes. 90+ nation members.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
notes: Current as of February 1, 2024. Three-tier structure: Canons, Ethical Standards, Rules of Conduct. Enforced by National Ethics Council.
Came into effect 1 May 2019 (revised 2018); supplementary guidance updated April 2021. Three principles: integrity, competence, relationships.

document_title: UIA Accord on Recommended International Standards of Professionalism in Architectural Practice — Policy on Ethics and Conduct
notes: Adopted Beijing June 1999; updated 2017. Intended as model code for UIA member sections.
Canon structure with Ethical Standards and mandatory Rules. ASLA also has a separate Code of Environmental Ethics.
Effective 2 February 2022. Applies globally to all RICS members and regulated firms. CPD requirement on ethics every 3 years. Previous version in place since 2007.
All FIDIC member associations subscribe to these principles. Promotes Quality-Based Selection (QBS) and anti-corruption stance.

document_title: Code of Ethics for the Professional Practice of Industrial Hygiene
notes: Provides standards for protecting health and well-being of working people. Board for Global EHS Credentialing (BGC) maintains an enforceable Code of Ethics.

document_title: The European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity (2023 Revised Edition)
notes: Published 23 June 2023. Recognised by European Commission as primary standard for Horizon-funded research. Increasingly serves as model for national codes globally. First edition 2011, revised 2017.

organization: World Conferences on Research Integrity Foundation
notes: Developed at 2nd World Conference on Research Integrity, Singapore, July 2010. 340 attendees from 51+ countries. 4 principles + 14 responsibilities. First international effort for unified research ethics policies.
Fosters values-based culture for ISC participants. Broader governance document for the world science community.

document_title: Declaration of Helsinki — Ethical Principles for Medical Research Involving Human Participants
notes: Originally adopted 1964; 8th revision adopted October 2024 (37 paragraphs). Cornerstone of human subjects research ethics globally.
Approved February 2011; replaced 1992 Ethical Standards. Nearly 3-year development process.

organization: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry / Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
document_title: Code of Ethical Principles of Chemistry
notes: Joint IUPAC-OPCW initiative. Focuses on dual-use chemistry and peaceful applications. Promotes ethics education in university chemistry curricula.
Voluntary principles emphasising truthfulness, substantiation, fair treatment, transparency, and privacy protection.
First adopted 1924. Prohibit false/misleading claims, offensive content, competitive disparagement. Unethical agencies denied membership.
Widely regarded as industry standard. No formal enforcement but membership may be restricted. Six core values + six code provisions of conduct.

document_title: ICCO Warsaw Principles — Ethical Use of AI in Public Relations and Communications
notes: Ratified at 2023 ICCO Global Summit in Warsaw. Represents 41 national PR associations across 82 countries, 3,000+ PR firms.

document_title: ICC/ESOMAR International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics
notes: Joint code since 1977. Mandatory for ESOMAR members; recognised by 60+ associations in 50+ countries. 2025 revision forthcoming.
In effect from 14 August 2023. Applies to all MRS members and Company Partners. Focuses on participant wellbeing, transparency, and inclusive data practices.

organization: AIGA — The Professional Association for Design
notes: Covers duties to clients, other designers, and society. Addresses fees, credit, conflicts of interest, and intellectual property.
Enforced by PPA Ethics Committee composed of PPA members.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Visual Journalists
notes: Emphasises truth, accuracy, and dignity. Prohibits staging photographs or manipulating news events.
Members agree to adhere as condition of membership. Emphasises professionalism, honesty, and respect for rights and dignity.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
notes: All ATA members must commit to CEPR. Sanctions list published. Covers honesty, competence, conflict of interest, confidentiality, accuracy.
Only global association of conference interpreters. Founded 1953; 3,000+ members in 100+ countries. Code revised 2022. Covers confidentiality, accuracy, dignity, working conditions, CPD.
Represents 80,000+ translators in 65 countries through 100+ associations. Code covers confidentiality, accuracy, integrity, and impartiality.

document_title: Principles of Veterinary Medical Ethics of the AVMA
notes: Three core principles: Stewardship, Integrity, Respect. Violation may result in AVMA disciplinary action. Most recent revision circulated 2024.

document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for Veterinary Surgeons
notes: Regulates under Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966. Statutory basis. Separate Code for Veterinary Nurses also exists. All vets take professional declaration on admission.
Aspirational/educational; state Veterinary Surgeons Boards hold regulatory enforcement authority. Four core values: professionalism, knowledge, community, adaptability.
Updated 2019 from 2012 original. Not legally binding unless enacted in national legislation. Sets common European veterinary ethical standards.
Updated 2025 to include stronger One Health, sustainability, and lifelong learning commitments. Used by national veterinary bodies worldwide as template for graduation oath.
